sources.note: Used only for its citation trail (Qu et al. 1989; Wang 2020; Suzuki & Nyima 2016; Tournadre 2014; Tournadre & Suzuki 2023; Jiang 2022; Qu & Jing 2017). Reproduces Qu et al. 1989: 50-51 wordlist with tone numerals; no stress statement.

sources.citation: Tournadre, Nicolas & Hiroyuki Suzuki. 2023. The Tibetic Languages: An introduction to the family of languages derived from Old Tibetan. Villejuif: LACITO Publications (Diversité des langues 1), 1151 pp. ISBN 978-2-490768-08-0.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Basum stress. Basum appears only in Chap. 10 (pp. 654-657: Charts X.4-X.6, lexical comparison with Classical Tibetan) and p. 680 (section 'Basum' in the Kongpo contact-language survey: location, name, legends, 'A description of Ba-ke has been written by Sanchuan Wang (2020)'). Basum forms are written with the book's word-pitch marks (ˉ high-level, ´ rising, ` falling, e.g. /ˉniː/ 'seven', /´kiː/ 'leg', /`ȵɐ/ 'fire'), which implies a pitch/tone notation but no explicit prosodic statement is made. Chap. 7 (phonology) covers Tibetic languages only, not Basum.

sources.note: p. 2: comparative wordlist with a Basum column (data 'from Nicolas Tournadre (p.c.), phonetic description reconfirmed by the first author'); Basum forms are given without pitch marks (ni 'seven', bər 'four', tɨʔ 'one', ŋo 'five'); no statement on Basum stress or tone.

sources.citation: Wang, Sanchuan. 2020. Phonologie et morphosyntaxe du Baké. Université Sorbonne Nouvelle - Paris 3 (dissertation; probably a Master's mémoire, cited as 'Doctoral dissertation' by Tournadre & Suzuki 2023: 1096).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only modern phonological description of Basum/Baké named anywhere; a 'Phonologie' section would settle whether Basum has tone, stress or both and where stress falls. Not deposited on theses.fr/HAL/DUMAS/SUDOC; may exist only at Paris 3 / with the author or supervisor (N. Tournadre).

sources.access_detail: only an abstract or snippet reachable
sources.note: Abstract and first paragraph only (CNKI; 23-page article behind paywall). Abstract: Basum is Tibetan, a fifth patois of the Ü-Tsang dialect, distinct because of a non-Tibetan lexical substratum close to Monpa; the article 'comprehensively introduces the features of Basong hua' by comparison with the four other Ü-Tsang patois. No stress information visible. (Wikipedia reproduces its wordlist pp. 50-51 with tone numerals 55/53/14/12/11, second-hand.)
